label: Smart TV / streaming
summary: 10-foot interface driven by a remote (D-pad), voice or controller
preview_screen: The home screen: a hero or featured item, two content rows, and the focused item clearly highlighted, inside the overscan safe zone.
required_screens: Search with on-screen keyboard (and voice prompt if voice is chosen)
required_states: Focus state on every focusable element
Focus moving between rows and columns
Error with a button to retry
design_guidance: Keep all content inside an overscan safe zone; a margin of about 5% on each edge is a common working default. Confirm against the chosen platform's guidelines.
Everything is operated by focus. Design a clear, high-contrast focus state (scale, outline or glow) for every focusable element; there is no cursor and no hover.
Design for distance: much larger type and fewer items per screen than desktop. Treat 24px body text at 1080p as a working minimum, not a target.
Navigation is spatial: up, down, left and right must land where users expect, with no focus traps and a consistent Back.
Avoid long text entry; offer voice, suggestions or a QR hand-off to the phone.

checks: No content or control sits in the overscan margin.
Every focusable element has a distinct focus state visible from a distance, with at least 3:1 contrast against its surroundings.
Every screen has an initial focus, and from it every control is reachable with the D-pad (no unreachable controls, no focus traps), and Back is always available.
Body text is large enough for the viewing distance (at or above the working minimum), and nothing relies on small captions.
No state depends on hover or on a pointer unless a pointer input was chosen.
Text entry has an alternative (voice, suggestions or hand-off) where long input is needed.
